assets.title: M87 in Legacy Surveys DR10 g, r, z colour cutout (DECam)

band.colourNote: Three optical/near-infrared DECam bands combined by the Legacy Surveys viewer's own colour mapping (legacypipe dr2_rgb / sdss_rgb, non-linear asinh-type stretch): g (about 480 nm) is shown blue, r (about 620 nm) green and z (about 900 nm, near-infrared) red. Because z lies beyond the visible range and the three bands are stretched non-linearly, this is a false-colour composite, not what an eye would see; it is the standard Legacy Surveys look. Brightness is not linear in flux. (Mapping z->red, g->blue confirmed by us: in the FITS cutout of the same field the z/g flux ratio correlates +0.73 with the JPEG's red-minus-blue.)

source.archive: Legacy Surveys (DESI Legacy Imaging Surveys) Sky Viewer cutout service

observation.telescope: Blanco 4-m telescope, CTIO (Dark Energy Camera, DECam); Legacy Surveys DR10 coadd
observation.date: Coadd of many exposures; epochs are not stated for the cutout

processing: Geometry is exact because we chose it: ra=187.7059, dec=12.3911, pixscale=0.5 arcsec/pixel, size=2048 pixels (field 1024 arcsec = 17.07 arcmin square), north up, east left, TAN. The JPEG itself has no header; we requested the FITS cutout of the same layer family (layer=ls-dr10, bands=grz) with identical parameters and read its header: CTYPE RA---TAN/DEC--TAN, CRVAL = 187.7059, 12.3911, CRPIX = 1024.5, 1024.5, CD1_1 = -1.388889e-4 deg (= -0.5 arcsec), CD2_2 = +1.388889e-4 deg, CD1_2 = CD2_1 = 0 (no rotation). The JPEG was checked to be on the same grid with north up (correlation of the FITS z band with the JPEG red channel at 16-pixel blocks: 0.84 north-up, 0.72 with the vertical flip).

Layer choice: 'ls-dr10-grz' (g, r, z only) rather than 'ls-dr10'/'ls-dr11', whose JPEG colour mapping in the DECam footprint includes the i band and whose DR10 JPEG of this field shows a purple masked streak; 'ls-dr11-grz' returned an empty image. The cutout is rendered by the Legacy Surveys service from its coadded DECam images; we did not coadd or calibrate anything.

The Legacy Surveys data licence page states that images are CC BY 4.0 and that the credit must read 'Legacy Surveys / D. Lang (Perimeter Institute)' unaltered, visible and with an active link online (https://www.legacysurvey.org/). Each survey layer has its own terms; for the Legacy Surveys layers this is the statement quoted in the licence evidence.

Limitations: saturated bright stars show diffraction spikes/coloured halos; M87's bright core and the faint outer halo are compressed by the non-linear stretch; this is a field of 17 arcmin, i.e. the inner galaxy only.

assets.title: M87 in GALEX NUV ultraviolet (SkyView)

band.colourNote: Single-band ultraviolet intensity shown as log-scaled greyscale; ultraviolet is invisible to the eye, and young hot stars dominate. No colour table applied. Contrast has been stretched by us (see processing) so faint structure is visible.

assets.credit: Data: GALEX (Galaxy Evolution Explorer), NASA, via the MAST GALEX archive; reprojected by NASA SkyView (HEASARC, NASA/GSFC).

licence.name: Public domain (as stated by SkyView for GALEX)
licence.evidence: SkyView survey description (also in the FITS header): 'Provenance: All data is downloaded from the MAST GALEX archive. Copyright: Public domain.'

observation.instrument: NUV channel, SkyView survey 'GALEX Near UV', bandpass 1.05-1.69 PHz

processing: Rendered by NASA SkyView from GALEX NUV mosaics with request parameters: Position=187.7059,12.3911, Survey=GALEX Near UV, Pixels=2048, Size=0.5, Projection=Tan, Coordinates=J2000, Return=JPEG, Scaling=Log, Sampler=LI, Cmap=Grey. Output is a TAN-projection greyscale JPEG, north up, east left, centred on the requested position (verified on a FITS request with the same geometry: CTYPE RA---TAN/DEC--TAN, CRVAL = request centre, CRPIX at image centre, CDELT1 negative, CDELT2 positive, no rotation).
Intensity is log-scaled by SkyView's JPEG writer with its default range; GALEX tile boundaries and exposure differences show as visible patches and noise.
